translationRepairs: In the jiaxu year Zhang Zhi rebelled at Jinzhou; Prince Muqali ordered him struck down, and in a fierce battle north of the city Botong was killed.
In the jiaxu year Zhang Zhi rebelled at Jinzhou; Prince Muqali ordered an attack on him, and in a fierce battle north of the city Botong was killed.

命擊之 takes 張致 as its object: Muqali ordered an attack on the Jinzhou rebel. “Ordered him struck down” both invites reading 之 as Botong and overtranslates 擊 as an execution. The replacement keeps the attack on Zhang Zhi and Botong’s death in the battle north of the city.

One night he went out in disguise and overheard townspeople saying: "Families are torn apart—parents from children, husbands from wives. The dead cannot return, and we have nothing with which to ransom the living. What can we do?"

One night he went out in disguise and overheard townspeople saying: "We have lost parents and children from one another. The dead cannot return, and we have nothing with which to ransom the living. What can we do?"
民間語 is 吾屬父母子女相失矣. 父母子女 names parents and children only; “husbands from wives” is invented. The replacement restores that kinship pair and 相失.

Once he went out at night in plain dress and heard people in the streets say: "We have lost parents, children, husbands and wives; the dead cannot live again, and the living have no means to ransom them—what is to be done!"

Once he went out at night in plain dress and heard people in the streets say: "We have lost parents and children from one another; the dead cannot live again, and the living have no means to ransom them—what is to be done!"
The literal line likewise inserts husbands and wives absent from 父母子女相失. “Lost parents and children from one another” matches the Chinese.
His family had been taken by Duke Ren and the rest, but Halabatu swore to stand or fall with the city."
Let my family be taken by you gentlemen; I, Halabatu, swear to stand or fall with the city."
s0075–s0076 are one speech (哈剌拔都曰…同存亡). 家屬任公等所俘 is the verb 任 plus address 公等, not a person 任公. The original invents Duke Ren and turns the hortative into past-tense narrative.
His family had been captured by Duke Ren and others; Halabatu swore to live or die with the city."
I leave my family to be captured by you gentlemen; Halabatu swears to live or die with the city."
The same clause is still inside the closing quotation. 任公等所俘 is permission that the addressees may take his family, not a report that Duke Ren had already captured them.

Temei and his son slipped over the wall by night to bring word of the revolt. Tianni's brother Tianze was returning from Beiping, met them outside the city, united the Mongol forces, drove south against the rebels, routed Wu Xian, and retook Zhending.

Temei and his son slipped over the wall by night to bring word of the revolt. Tianni's brother Tianze was returning from Beijing, met them at Mancheng, united the Mongol forces, drove south against the rebels, routed Wu Xian, and retook Zhending.

遇諸滿城 is the county Mancheng, not “outside the city,” and 還自北京 is Beijing, not anachronistic Beiping. The supplied window still writes 忒末 as Temei in s0107; changing only this sentence to Teme is an unsupported spelling swap, so Temei is kept.

Father and son Temei by night climbed over the wall and went out, intending to report the matter. Just then Tianni's younger brother Tianze returned from Beiping, met them outside the full city, united the Mongol armies southward to fight the rebels, put Wu Xian to flight, and recovered Zhending.

Father and son Temei by night climbed over the wall and went out, intending to report the matter. Just then Tianni's younger brother Tianze returned from Beijing, met them at Mancheng, united the Mongol armies southward to fight the rebels, put Wu Xian to flight, and recovered Zhending.

滿城 is the place-name Mancheng, not “the full city,” and 北京 is Beijing. The proposal’s further change of Temei to Teme is not required by 忒末 in this unit and would diverge from the following sentence’s Temei.
He was made General Who Upholds the State, campaign marshal of Mozhou, and concurrent pacification commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.
He was made General Who Upholds the State, campaign marshal of Mingzhou, and concurrent pacification commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.
加…洺州征行元帥 is Mingzhou (洺), not Mozhou (莫). The replacement restores the prefecture in the title.
He was promoted to General Who Upholds the State, campaigning marshal of Mozhou, and concurrently pacification commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.
He was promoted to General Who Upholds the State, campaigning marshal of Mingzhou, and concurrently pacification commissioner of Zhao Prefecture.
The literal office string has the same misreading of 洺州 as Mozhou. Mingzhou is the correct place.
His grandson Shi Jie served as Court Gentleman for Attendance and chief transport commissioner for the Jiangxi tea monopoly.
His grandson Shi Yi served as Court Gentleman for Attendance and chief transport commissioner for the Jiangxi tea monopoly.
孫世枻 uses 枻 (yì), not 傑/杰. Shi Jie is a wrong reading of the given name; Shi Yi matches the graph.
Six sons—Qiyuli, Qizhijian, Qizhedu, Qichaowu, and Qiliechi—each earned the jinshi degree.
He had six sons; Qiyuli, Qizhijian, Qizhedu, Qichaowu, and Qiliechi each earned the jinshi degree.

子六人 is followed by five personal names and 皆第進士. The em-dash list makes those five names the complete set of six sons. A semicolon keeps the count of six and the five named jinshi without equating them.
He had six sons—Qiyuli, Qizhijian, Qizhedu, Qichaowu, and Qiliechi—all of whom passed the jinshi examination.
He had six sons; Qiyuli, Qizhijian, Qizhedu, Qichaowu, and Qiliechi all passed the jinshi examination.
The literal dash-list has the same false equation of five names with 子六人. The semicolon repair matches the Chinese syntax.

Starting as a translation clerk in the Secretariat, he became assistant administrator of the Dongping Chief Administrator's office, then of the Chief Transport Office, and served as prefect of Guanzhou and then Xuzhou, winning a record of good governance everywhere he went.

Starting as a translation clerk in the Secretariat, he became assistant administrator of the Dongping Chief Administrator's office, then of the Chief Transport Office, and served as prefect of Guanzhou and then Xu prefecture, winning a record of good governance everywhere he went.
再知許州 is Xu prefecture (許州), not 徐州. English Xuzhou names the wrong place; Xu prefecture keeps the two graphs distinct.
He posted the assistant administrator Sunbotiemuer at Fenyin, the investigating officer Cheng Qian at Yumen, and the Hedong County magistrate Wang Weny at the Fengling crossings.
He posted the assistant administrator Sunbotiemuer at Fenyin, the investigating officer Cheng Qian at Yumen, and the Hedong County magistrate Wang Wenyi at the Fengling crossings.
河東縣尹王文義 is Wang Wenyi. Weny drops the 義 syllable and is not a complete reading of the given name.

He ordered the assistant administrator Sunbotiemuer to hold Fenyin, the investigating officer Cheng Qian to hold Yumen, and the Hedong County magistrate Wang Weny to hold the crossings at Fengling and elsewhere.

He ordered the assistant administrator Sunbotiemuer to hold Fenyin, the investigating officer Cheng Qian to hold Yumen, and the Hedong County magistrate Wang Wenyi to hold the crossings at Fengling and elsewhere.
The literal line repeats Wang Weny for 王文義. Wang Wenyi restores both syllables of 文義.

He was posthumously made Merit Subject Who Pushes Sincerity and Upholds Integrity, Palace Attendant, pacification commissioner of the Hedong-Shanxi Circuit, protector of the army, and Marquis of Pengcheng Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.

He was posthumously made Merit Subject Who Pushes Sincerity and Upholds Integrity, Zhongfeng Grand Master, pacification commissioner of the Hedong-Shanxi Circuit, protector of the army, and Marquis of Pengcheng Commandery, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.
中奉大夫 is the prestige rank Zhongfeng Grand Master, not Palace Attendant (侍中 and similar). The rest of the posthumous string is unchanged.
